div.l: Ther to he strong was / as a champioıı̄un
He knewe the ta verys verys taverys / vel in euery touıı̄un
And eủery hosteler / and tapstere
Bet than a lazeer / or a begstere
For vn to such a worthi man as he
Accordith nat / as bi his faculte
To have with syk Lazerys acqueyntaıı̄unce
It is nat honest / it may nat avaıı̄unce
For to delyn / with such porayle
But al with riche / and selleres of vitayle
And overal ther / as profyt shulde a ryse
Curteyse he was / and lowlych of ʆseruyce
Ther was no man̄ / nowher so vertuous
He was the beste beggere of his hows
For thow a wydowe / hadde but a sho
So plesaunt / was his Inpⁱrincipio
Yeet wolde he have / a ferthyng er / than he wente
His purchas was wel better / than his rente
And rage he cowde / right as it were a whelp ·
In love dayes / ther / kowde he mechel help ·
For ther he was / nat lyk a cloystrere
With thredbare coope / as is a pore scolere
But he was lyke a mayster or a pope
Of dowble worstede / was his semy cope
That was rownde / as a belle out of the presse
Somwhat he lypsed / for his wantoıı̄unnesse
To maken his englyssh swete vp on his tonge
And in his harpyng /whan he had songe
His eyen twynkeled in his hede a ryht
As doth the sterres / in the frosty nyht
This worthi lymytour / was cleped hoberd
A MarchantA Marchaunt was ther / with a forked berd
In motle / and hye on hors he sat
Vp on his hede a flaıı̄undryssh beuer hat
His botys clapsed / fayre and fetysly
